pr.title: Spec one loop that fixes and reviews pull requests
pr.head: 5c69842c18178fa6d4f0169e81a9081bf8d80ad7

summary: Projector drives a pull request to a clean review with two background loops. The watch loop runs in the session that opened a pull request and fixes the review findings that arrive on it. The review loop runs once per repository and reviews every new head of the operator's pull requests, keeping each one a draft until a review finds its head clean. Each loop runs a bash watcher that queries GitHub's GraphQL API for every pull request on every pass, whether or not anything changed.

That polling spends a quota GitHub shares across every session and machine on the account: 5,000 GraphQL points an hour. At 10 pull requests and a 60-second interval, the two loops spend about 2,000 points an hour, and the quota has run out in practice.

This pull request adds a plan, not code. The plan merges both loops into one skill, start-pr-loop, backed by a new CLI command, project loop watch. Each pull request in the loop's tracked file gets a fix role, a review role, or both. Each pass asks GitHub a conditional REST question per pull request, which is free when GitHub answers 304 Not Modified, and runs the GraphQL query only for a pull request that changed, plus a full pass every 10 minutes. One loop per repository and model holds the review role through a lease: a file lock that the operating system releases when the holder's watcher ends. The plan estimates about 210 GraphQL points an hour at 10 pull requests.

The plan is at draft with priority now. It leaves four choices to the owner in § 7: whether the loop lives in the CLI, whether every loop competes for the review role, how two machines share it, and the skill's name.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Operator: the GitHub account gh is signed in as.
  • Tracked file: a loop's list of owner/repo#number lines, its whole scope. A ! line keeps a pull request out.
  • Conditional request: a REST request that sends the resource's last ETag in If-None-Match, so GitHub answers 304 when nothing changed.
  • Lease: the right to hold the review role for one repository and model, held through an exclusive lock on a file.
  • Handover: another loop taking the lease once the holder's watcher ends, along with its review lines.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:
The first review of this head opened two findings, both on the handover in § 2.4:

  • Review state and its lock live per machine, so a holder that ends mid-review leaves a lock that refuses the new holder's setup on that head.
  • A ! line has no role, so the handover loses a review dismissal or turns a fix dismissal into one.

groups.title: The pr-loop plan
groups.kicker: One new plan: the merged loop, its conditional polling, and the review lease
intro: The plan follows the repository's plan layout: the problem in § 1, the design in § 2, the reasons in § 3, then acceptance criteria, cost, rollout, open questions, and the measurements behind its claims. § 2 carries the substance. § 2.1 walks one pass, § 2.2 lists the conditional requests and marks which of their behaviors were observed and which are inferred, § 2.3 adds roles to the tracked file, and § 2.4 defines the review lease.
Read § 2.4 most closely. The lease decides which session reviews, and its handover moves review work between sessions on one machine, where the review commands already keep state of their own.

files.note: The new plan for one loop that fixes and reviews pull requests.

checks.text: The cost figures hold: the watch watcher's query costs 1 point and the review watcher's 2 by GitHub's documented formula, giving about 2,000 points an hour for both at 10 pull requests.
A live conditional request for this pull request answered HTTP/2.0 304 Not Modified, made gh api exit 1, and left X-Ratelimit-Used unchanged, as the plan says.
This query is the union of the two watchers' queries, so one result serves both roles. It still costs 2 points.
A role-less line stays the fix role, so a watcher from an earlier release still reads a file that project loop add wrote.
A ! line keeps a pull request out of every role. At a handover, a review dismissal is lost when the taker fixes the pull request, and the taker's own fix dismissal stops the pull request's reviews.

Review state and its lock are per machine. A holder that ends mid-review leaves a lock that refuses the taker's project review setup on that head for up to a day, and a loop that loses the role and runs project review finish --force would delete the taker's review.
The four questions marked Owner, before implementation keep the plan at draft.
